title: readSTL
body:
## readSTL

Imports one triangle mesh from an STL file with Blender's STL importer, multiplying coordinates by scale and keeping the file's axes (Y forward, Z up, scene units ignored). STL carries no unit information, so scale is how you convert: 0.001 turns a millimetre CAD export into metre-sized Blender units. The file is copied into the run directory and its digest checked.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The file must produce exactly one mesh object with faces; otherwise UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE.
- scale is a constant set at creation; it cannot vary with an $axis. Use transform for varying scale.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `readSTL`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | Path of the STL file to import. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process; in workflows an $artifact from a verified producer is usual. The file is copied into the run directory and both copies are digest-checked; it is fixed when the node is created. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1}` | **required** |
| `scale` | Uniform factor applied to every imported coordinate (importer global_scale; scene units ignored). STL stores bare numbers, so this is how you set units: 0.001 makes a millimetre export metre-sized, 1 keeps the numbers. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1e-06,"maximum":1000000}` | `1` |

- `file` is a constructor option.
- `scale` is a constructor option.
